name: live_data
description: Use when you need the current value of an engine sensor (a Mode 01 PID), read once or sampled for a few seconds for min / avg / max.
instructions: Call read_live with up to 8 Mode 01 PIDs, e.g. {"pids":["010C","0105"]}.
Which PIDs exist on this car comes from the tool's "Not supported on this car" line: do not ask for those PIDs again, choose another way to check.
seconds 0 (or left out) reads once. seconds > 0 (up to 15) samples every 0.5 s and gives min / avg / max: use it to judge whether a value is steady, swinging or drifting.
Read the values the symptom points at, e.g. rpm 010C, coolant 0105, load 0104, MAP 010B, MAF 0110, speed 010D, module voltage 0142, fuel trims 0106 / 0107.
interpret: One reading is one moment: sample a few seconds before calling a value unstable.
Warm engine coolant: about 80-105 °C. Under 70 °C after a long drive points to a thermostat stuck open; over 110 °C is overheating.
Warm idle: usually 700-900 rpm. A min-max swing over about 100 rpm while sampling points to an unstable idle.
MAP (010B) at idle: close to barometric pressure (about 100 kPa) on a diesel, about 25-45 kPa on a petrol engine.
Fuel trims (0106 / 0107) within ±10 % are normal; beyond +20 % points to lean (air leak, low fuel delivery), beyond -20 % to rich.
Module voltage (0142) with the engine running: 13.5-14.5 V means the alternator charges; under 13 V it does not.
